toegepas.voor: soos Ra die songod en Anubis
toegepas.na: soos die songod Ra en Anubis
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Ra die songod' is an apposition without its commas, unlike 'Anubis, die god van mummifisering'; putting the title first is natural and needs no extra commas before 'en'.
toegepas.fout: 'Ra die songod en Anubis, die god van mummifisering' has an uncommaed apposition next to a commaed one, so a reader can stumble and read 'Ra, die songod en Anubis' as three items.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Putting the title first removes the stumble and keeps the two gods parallel without changing meaning; the protected words 'Ra' and 'songod' stay intact.

toegepas.blok: Leer by die huis en op skool
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Skoolgaan' is one verb (AWS), so its past participle is written 'skoolgegaan'; 'Net sommige kinders' and 'veral uit ryk families' stay untouched.
toegepas.fout: 'skoolgaan' is written as one word by the AWS, so the past participle is 'skoolgegaan', not 'skool gegaan'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: A plain spelling fix that leaves the protected quantifiers 'Net sommige kinders' and 'veral uit ryk families' untouched.

na_skrywer.na: bordspeletjies, net soos die antieke Egiptenare
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'bordspeletjies soos die Egiptenare' can be misread as 'board games such as the Egyptians'; 'net soos' with a comma makes the comparison cover both clauses, and 'antieke' separates them from Egyptians today in a then-and-now block.
na_skrywer.fout: 'bordspeletjies soos die Egiptenare' can first be read as 'board games such as the Egyptians', because 'soos' after a plural noun introduces examples elsewhere in this lesson; in a then-and-now block 'die Egiptenare' can also be read as Egyptians today.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The ambiguity is real, but the proposal adds 'antieke' and strengthens the comparison to 'net soos' across both clauses, which moves the claim, so the writer should choose the fix.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

vlae.teks: Vis uit die Nyl was vir hulle belangrik.
vlae.rede: 'hulle' could refer to the farmer's family or to both the farmer's family and the rich family in the previous sentence; naming the intended group would mean guessing the content, so the writer should decide.
